h.strategy: Before proposing, briefly model the system: which components carry most of the signal, which are redundant, and where saturation, bottlenecks or substitution between components could occur. Then propose hypotheses that each test a DIFFERENT mechanism (e.g., redundancy, saturation/diminishing returns, bottleneck, interference, compensation, sign reversal). Prefer interactions where the intuitive answer is plausibly wrong, including cases where a usually helpful edit should help LESS or even hurt. Use varied edit fields, condition fields and both directions; no two hypotheses may share the same edit-condition pair or the same underlying reason. Each 'why' must name a concrete mechanism and what pattern would falsify it, not just say a component 'matters more'.

hyps.why: With edge 1 absent, edge 0 is the sole entry into the node1/node2 sub-network, so its capacity matters more.
A direct skip keeps input-to-output connectivity so cutting edge 0 is less damaging.
With edge 0 none, node 1 is dead so removing edge 2 is inert, whereas otherwise it removes a useful path.
A parallel weak conv adds little when the input already feeds a 3x3 conv.
Chaining conv3x3 on edge 0 into edge 2 builds a deeper path with larger receptive field.
With edge 4 absent, edge 5 is a main deep route to the output so removing it hurts more.
A strong deep route already supplies conv features so a shallow conv on edge 3 adds less.
With edge 1 none, edge 2 is node 2's only input so cutting it also kills edge 5's path.
With no direct path, a skip on edge 4 gives the only short route from node 1 to the output.
Two parallel 3x3 convs into the output overlap in function so the second adds less.
